name: v10_doubtful_receivables_allowance_quality
hypothesis: Higher allowance for doubtful receivables relative to sales can indicate collection risk and lower revenue quality. Use a light profitability anchor, but keep the receivables-quality term dominant.
expression: 0.70 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * fn_allowance_for_doubtful_accounts_receivable_a / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.30 * group_rank(ts_rank(operating_income / assets, 126), subindustry)
notes: Extension of the successful v9 receivables/sales branch, but uses doubtful-account allowance rather than total receivables.

name: v10_trade_receivables_cashflow_quality
hypothesis: High trade receivables relative to sales is risky when cash-flow quality is not strong. Mix trade receivables with CFO/assets to reduce dependence on the exact v9 receivable field.
expression: 0.55 * group_rank(ts_rank(-1 * fnd6_rectr / sales, 126), subindustry) + 0.30 * group_rank(ts_rank(cash_flow_from_operations / assets, 126), industry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(operating_income / assets, 126), subindustry)
notes: Designed to test receivable-quality plus cash conversion rather than simply reusing total receivables/sales.

name: v10_receivable_decrease_cashflow
hypothesis: Accounts receivable decrease relative to sales can signal improving cash conversion. Combine with CFO/assets as a slow cash-quality mechanism.
notes: Direction follows the field description: 'Accounts Receivable - Decrease (Increase)'. Submit only if correlation with v9 receivables is clearly below threshold.

name: v10_competitor_hub_quality_no_reversal
hypothesis: Competitor graph hub score may capture a different network role than competitor authority. Keep no close/open reversal to avoid repeating the v8 parent-fusion structure.
notes: Sibling of the successful v9 competitor authority alpha; strict correlation gate should block it if hub and authority are too close.

name: v10_competitor_customer_spread_quality
hypothesis: Competitor authority and customer authority describe different network positions. A spread may isolate firms that are central among competitors without being merely a customer-network clone.
expression: 0.55 * group_rank(ts_rank(pv13_com_rk_au, 60), industry) - 0.30 * group_rank(ts_rank(pv13_ustomergraphrank_auth_rank, 60), industry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(operating_income / assets, 126), subindustry)
notes: Designed as a graph-spread mechanism, not a pure authority near-neighbor.

name: v10_customer_breadth_cashflow_quality
hypothesis: More customer relationships can indicate diversified demand, but it needs cash-flow quality to avoid low-margin breadth. This tests a graph-count signal rather than graph-rank centrality.
expression: 0.60 * group_rank(ts_rank(rel_num_cust, 60), industry) + 0.25 * group_rank(ts_rank(cash_flow_from_operations / assets, 126), industry) + 0.15 * group_rank(ts_rank(operating_income / assets, 126), subindustry)
notes: Uses relationship breadth; expected to be distinct from v7/v9 authority if it works.
